title: Judges Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 14.

questions.question: Where did Samson go down to see a woman of the daughters of the Philistines?
options: Timnath
Jerusalem
Bethlehem
Hebron
questions.correctAnswer: Timnath
questions.explanation: Samson went down to Timnath to see a woman of the daughters of the Philistines as mentioned in Judges 14:1.

questions.question: Who did Samson tell about the woman he saw in Timnath?
options: His father and mother
His brothers
The elders of Israel
The Philistine leaders
questions.correctAnswer: His father and mother
questions.explanation: Samson told his father and mother about the woman in Timnath as stated in Judges 14:2.

questions.question: What was Samson's parents' reaction to his desire to marry a Philistine woman?
options: They questioned why he would choose an uncircumcised Philistine woman
They immediately agreed and arranged the marriage
They forbade him from marrying her
They told him to marry a woman from another tribe
questions.correctAnswer: They questioned why he would choose an uncircumcised Philistine woman
questions.explanation: His parents asked if there was no woman among their own people before he chose a Philistine, as seen in Judges 14:3.

questions.question: Did Samson's parents know that the LORD was using his marriage to seek an occasion against the Philistines?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The text says his father and mother did not know it was of the LORD that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, implying the LORD was orchestrating it, but his parents were unaware, which confirms the statement is true from their perspective in Judges 14:4.

questions.question: What did Samson and his parents encounter in the vineyards of Timnath?
options: A young lion roaring
A Philistine army
A wedding feast
An angel of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: A young lion roaring
questions.explanation: They came to the vineyards of Timnath where a young lion roared against Samson according to Judges 14:5.

questions.question: How did Samson kill the lion?
options: With a sword
With a spear
By tearing it apart with his hands
With a trap
questions.correctAnswer: By tearing it apart with his hands
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson and he rent the lion as he would have rent a kid, with no weapon in his hand, as told in Judges 14:6.

questions.question: Did Samson tell his parents about killing the lion?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Samson did not tell his father or mother what he had done when he killed the lion (Judges 14:6).

questions.question: What was Samson's impression of the woman he spoke with in Timnath?
options: She pleased him well
He was indifferent to her
He disliked her
He was afraid of her
questions.correctAnswer: She pleased him well
questions.explanation: Judges 14:7 states that Samson went down and talked with the woman and she pleased him well.

questions.question: What did Samson find inside the carcass of the lion when he returned?
options: A swarm of bees and honey
A hidden treasure
A nest of snakes
Nothing
questions.correctAnswer: A swarm of bees and honey
questions.explanation: When Samson returned, he found a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass of the lion, as described in Judges 14:8.

questions.question: Did Samson reveal to his parents that he took honey from the lion's carcass?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: He gave honey to his parents to eat but did not tell them that it came from the lion's carcass according to Judges 14:9.

questions.question: What kind of feast did Samson make when his father went down to the woman?
options: A wedding feast
A feast for young men as was their custom
A sacrifice feast
A harvest feast
questions.correctAnswer: A feast for young men as was their custom
questions.explanation: Judges 14:10 states that Samson made a feast for the young men, for so they used to do.

questions.question: How many companions did the men bring when they saw Samson?
questions.explanation: When the men saw Samson, they brought thirty companions to be with him according to Judges 14:11.

questions.question: What did Samson propose to the men during the feast?
options: A riddle with a reward for solving it
A wrestling match
A feast competition
A battle challenge
questions.correctAnswer: A riddle with a reward for solving it
questions.explanation: Samson proposed a riddle to the men with a prize for solving it as related in Judges 14:12.

questions.question: In which order did these events occur? 1) Samson kills the lion, 2) Samson sees the woman in Timnath, 3) Samson speaks the riddle at the feast, 4) Samson finds honey in the lion's carcass.
questions.explanation: Samson first saw the woman (verse 1), then killed the lion (verse 6), found honey in the carcass (verse 8), and finally spoke the riddle at the feast (verse 12).

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of the LORD did not come upon Samson during his encounter with the lion.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson when he killed the lion (Judges 14:6), so the statement is false.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Samson find inside the carcass of the lion when he returned to take his wife?
options: A swarm of bees and honey
A nest of snakes
A hidden treasure
A flock of birds
questions.correctAnswer: A swarm of bees and honey
questions.explanation: Judges 14:8 describes Samson turning aside to see the carcass of the lion and finding a swarm of bees and honey inside it.

questions.question: How did Samson share the honey he found in the lion’s carcass?
options: He ate it alone in secret
He gave it to his father and mother to eat
He sold it to the Philistines
He gave it to the woman he was going to marry
questions.correctAnswer: He gave it to his father and mother to eat
questions.explanation: Judges 14:9 states that Samson took the honey in his hands, ate it, then gave some to his father and mother, though he did not tell them the source.

questions.question: What custom did Samson follow when he made a feast at Timnath?
options: He made a sacrifice to the LORD
He held a feast as young men used to do
He invited only family members
He fasted and prayed before the feast
questions.correctAnswer: He held a feast as young men used to do
questions.explanation: Judges 14:10 explains that Samson made a feast, as was the custom for young men at that time.

questions.question: How many companions did Samson’s future wife bring to the feast?
options: Ten
Twenty
Thirty
Forty
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty
questions.explanation: Judges 14:11 clearly states that when they saw Samson, they brought thirty companions to be with him at the feast.

questions.question: What reward did Samson offer if the companions could solve his riddle within seven days?
options: Thirty sheets and thirty change of garments
Thirty gold coins
Thirty cattle
Thirty servants
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty sheets and thirty change of garments
questions.explanation: Judges 14:12 records Samson promising thirty sheets and thirty changes of garments if they declared the riddle correctly within seven days.

questions.question: What would the companions have to give Samson if they failed to solve his riddle?
options: Thirty sheets and thirty change of garments
Thirty gold coins
Thirty cattle
Thirty servants
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty sheets and thirty change of garments
questions.explanation: Judges 14:13 states that if they could not declare the riddle, they had to give Samson thirty sheets and thirty change of garments.

questions.question: What was the content of Samson's riddle?
options: Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?
Who is the greatest king?
What is the sound of one hand clapping?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness
questions.explanation: Judges 14:14 contains the exact words of Samson’s riddle, which references the honey from the lion’s carcass.

questions.question: What did the companions fail to do within the first three days of the feast?
options: They failed to expound the riddle
They failed to attend the feast
They failed to bring gifts
They failed to invite Samson’s wife
questions.correctAnswer: They failed to expound the riddle
questions.explanation: Judges 14:14 states that they could not expound the riddle within three days, showing their inability to solve it quickly.

questions.question: What threat did the companions make to Samson’s wife to get the answer to the riddle?
options: They threatened to burn her and her father's house with fire
They threatened to exile her from the city
They threatened to imprison Samson
They threatened to take her children
questions.correctAnswer: They threatened to burn her and her father's house with fire
questions.explanation: Judges 14:15 describes how the companions threatened Samson’s wife to entice him to tell the riddle or face burning her and her father's house.

questions.question: How did Samson respond when his wife accused him of hating her because he would not tell her the riddle?
options: He said he had not told his father or mother and would not tell her
He apologized and told her the riddle
He ignored her and left the feast
He told her to ask the companions instead
questions.correctAnswer: He said he had not told his father or mother and would not tell her
questions.explanation: Judges 14:16 records Samson telling his wife that he had not told his father or mother, so he would not tell her either.

questions.question: What caused Samson to finally reveal the riddle to his wife?
options: She wept before him for seven days and lay sore upon him
He felt sorry for her after the feast
He was angry and wanted to punish the companions
He wanted to end the feast early
questions.correctAnswer: She wept before him for seven days and lay sore upon him
questions.explanation: Judges 14:17 explains that after she wept and pressed him for seven days, he told her the riddle.

questions.question: What was Samson’s response when the men of the city solved the riddle?
options: If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle
You have cheated and broken the agreement
I will give you the promised garments
I will cancel the feast
questions.correctAnswer: If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle
questions.explanation: Judges 14:18 records Samson’s response, accusing them of cheating by involving his wife.

questions.question: What happened after the Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson following the riddle's exposure?
options: He went down to Ashkelon, slew thirty men, and took their spoil
He fled the city to avoid conflict
He made peace with the Philistines
He returned home quietly
questions.correctAnswer: He went down to Ashkelon, slew thirty men, and took their spoil
questions.explanation: Judges 14:19 describes how the Spirit of the LORD empowered Samson to kill thirty men and take their spoil after the riddle was exposed.

questions.question: What happened to Samson's wife after the riddle incident?
options: She was given to Samson’s companion
She remained with Samson
She returned to her father's house
She was sent to another city
questions.correctAnswer: She was given to Samson’s companion
questions.explanation: Judges 14:20 states that Samson’s wife was given to his companion, showing the fallout of the riddle's betrayal.

questions.question: True or False: Samson’s parents understood that his desire to marry a Philistine woman was part of God’s plan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 14:4 makes clear that Samson’s parents did not know it was of the LORD that he sought an occasion against the Philistines.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 14.

questions.question: What threat did the men of the city make to Samson's wife to entice Samson to reveal the riddle?
options: They threatened to burn her and her father's house
They threatened to kill Samson's wife
They threatened to imprison Samson
They threatened to exile Samson's wife
questions.correctAnswer: They threatened to burn her and her father's house
questions.explanation: Judges 14:15 states that they threatened to burn her and her father's house if she did not entice Samson to reveal the riddle.

questions.question: How did Samson respond when his wife wept and asked him to reveal the riddle?
options: He told her immediately
He refused, saying he had not told even his parents
He threatened to leave her
He told her a different riddle
questions.correctAnswer: He refused, saying he had not told even his parents
questions.explanation: Judges 14:16 explains that Samson said he had not told the riddle to his father or mother and questioned why he should tell her.

questions.question: For how many days did Samson's wife weep before he finally told her the riddle?
options: Three days
Five days
Seven days
Ten days
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Judges 14:17 states that she wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted until he told her on the seventh day.

questions.question: What was the riddle Samson posed to the men of the city?
options: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness"
"What is the beginning and end of all things?"
"Who can ascend to heaven without dying?"
"What walks on four legs in the morning?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness"
questions.explanation: Judges 14:14 records Samson's riddle involving the lion and honey in the carcass.

questions.question: What was the significance of Samson’s phrase, 'If ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle'?
options: It meant they had discovered the riddle by force
It referred to Samson’s wife betraying him
It indicated a farming metaphor unrelated to the riddle
It was a challenge to their agricultural skills
questions.correctAnswer: It referred to Samson’s wife betraying him
questions.explanation: Judges 14:18 implies that the men found out the riddle because Samson’s wife (his 'heifer') revealed it to them.

questions.question: What happened after the men of the city solved Samson's riddle?
options: Samson fled the city immediately
Samson slew thirty men of Ashkelon and gave their garments to the riddle solvers
Samson was imprisoned by the men
The men of the city gave Samson gifts
questions.correctAnswer: Samson slew thirty men of Ashkelon and gave their garments to the riddle solvers
questions.explanation: Judges 14:19 states that Samson, empowered by the Spirit of the LORD, killed thirty men and gave their spoils as payment for the riddle being solved.

questions.question: What was done with Samson’s wife after the riddle event?
options: She remained with Samson
She was given to Samson’s companion
She fled to her father's house
She married another Philistine man
questions.correctAnswer: She was given to Samson’s companion
questions.explanation: Judges 14:20 says Samson’s wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as a friend.

questions.question: The riddle in Judges 14:14 employs which literary device by contrasting 'eater' and 'strong' with 'meat' and 'sweetness'?
options: Chiasm
Parallelism
Metaphor
Irony
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The structure of the riddle in Judges 14:14 is chiastic, contrasting eater/meat and strong/sweetness in a mirrored pattern, a common Hebrew literary device.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine empowerment seen when 'the Spirit of the LORD came upon' Samson in Judges 14:19?
options: Numbers 11:25 - The Spirit enabling the seventy elders
Genesis 1:2 - The Spirit moving over the waters
Exodus 20:2 - The giving of the Ten Commandments
Psalm 23:1 - The Lord as shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 11:25 - The Spirit enabling the seventy elders
questions.explanation: Like Judges 14:19 where the Spirit empowers Samson for strength, Numbers 11:25 describes the Spirit of the LORD coming upon the elders to empower them.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'riddle' in Judges 14:12 is 'חידה' (chidah). What is the primary meaning of this word in the Old Testament context?
options: A difficult enigma or puzzle to be solved
A prophetic vision
A joyful song
A legal decree
questions.correctAnswer: A difficult enigma or puzzle to be solved
questions.explanation: The Hebrew 'chidah' commonly means a riddle or enigmatic saying that requires interpretation, as in Judges 14:12 where Samson challenges others to solve it.

questions.question: What historical context is important for understanding Samson’s marriage to a Philistine woman in Judges 14:1-3?
options: The Philistines were oppressing Israel at the time
The Philistines were allies of Israel
The Philistines were descendants of Israel
The Philistines had no interaction with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines were oppressing Israel at the time
questions.explanation: Judges 14:4 explains the Philistines had dominion over Israel, making Samson’s marriage politically and culturally significant.

questions.question: How does Samson’s riddle and subsequent conflict foreshadow his later role as a judge in Israel?
options: It shows his strength and conflict with Philistines
It predicts his peaceful reign over Israel
It indicates his role as a priest
It foreshadows his exile from Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It shows his strength and conflict with Philistines
questions.explanation: Judges 14:19 shows Samson empowered by God’s Spirit to defeat enemies, prefiguring his leadership against the Philistines as a judge.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references Samson as an example of faith and strength, connecting to his story in Judges 14?
options: Hebrews 11:32
Romans 5:1
John 1:1
Acts 2:38
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:32
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:32 mentions Samson among the heroes of faith, linking to his exploits including those in Judges 14.

questions.question: True or False: Samson immediately told his wife the riddle when she first asked him during the feast.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: According to Judges 14:16-17, Samson initially refused and only told her on the seventh day after much weeping.

questions.question: True or False: The Spirit of the LORD coming upon Samson enabled him to kill thirty men in Ashkelon as described in Judges 14.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 14:19 explicitly states that the Spirit of the LORD came upon Samson and he slew thirty men of Ashkelon.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine purpose is revealed by Samson's desire to marry a Philistine woman, despite his parents' objections?
options: Samson sought to rebel against his family
It was of the LORD to seek occasion against the Philistines
He wanted to unite Israel and Philistines through marriage
Samson was unaware of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: It was of the LORD to seek occasion against the Philistines
questions.explanation: Judges 14:4 states that Samson's parents did not know that it was of the LORD that he sought an occasion against the Philistines, revealing God's sovereign purpose through Samson's actions.

questions.question: What does Samson’s killing of the lion without any weapon (Judges 14:6) demonstrate about the Spirit of the LORD?
options: The Spirit enables natural abilities
The Spirit empowers supernatural strength
The Spirit encourages violence
The Spirit punishes enemies directly
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit empowers supernatural strength
questions.explanation: Judges 14:6 describes the Spirit of the LORD coming mightily upon Samson, enabling him to tear the lion apart with his bare hands, illustrating divine empowerment beyond human capability.

questions.question: How does the riddle Samson poses at his wedding feast reflect the theme of God’s hidden wisdom and revelation?
options: It reveals God's judgment on Israel
It symbolizes the mystery of Christ’s victory
It shows human wisdom surpassing divine knowledge
It is a simple folk tale with no deeper meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the mystery of Christ’s victory
questions.explanation: The riddle 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness' (Judges 14:14) symbolically reflects how victory and blessing come from apparent death and strength, a typology pointing to Christ's triumph.

questions.question: What does Samson’s secrecy about the honey from the lion’s carcass (Judges 14:9) teach about human nature in relation to divine mysteries?
options: Humans always share divine truths openly
Humans often conceal divine acts for personal gain
Humans can be reluctant to reveal God’s workings
Humans reject divine signs completely
questions.correctAnswer: Humans can be reluctant to reveal God’s workings
questions.explanation: Judges 14:9 shows Samson eating honey from the lion’s carcass and not telling his parents about it, illustrating human hesitation or secrecy regarding the revelation of God’s miraculous works.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted by the Spirit coming upon Samson to enable his victory and deliverance from the Philistines?
options: God’s omniscience
God’s omnipotence
God’s immutability
God’s justice
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence
questions.explanation: The Spirit of the LORD coming upon Samson to give him extraordinary power (Judges 14:6, 19) reveals God's omnipotence in enabling deliverance through human agents.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from the combination of Judges 14:4 and Judges 14:19 regarding God’s sovereignty and human agency?
options: God controls only natural events, not human decisions
God uses human actions for divine purposes despite human intentions
Human actions always contradict God’s will
God’s sovereignty excludes human responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human actions for divine purposes despite human intentions
questions.explanation: Judges 14:4 shows God’s sovereign plan through Samson’s marriage desire, and Judges 14:19 shows the Spirit empowering Samson to slay Philistines, together teaching that God sovereignly works through human actions even when humans do not fully understand.

questions.question: How does Samson’s giving of garments to those who solved the riddle (Judges 14:19) reflect on the biblical doctrine of covenant obligations and promises?
options: It exemplifies breaking of vows
It represents the fulfillment of a sworn covenant
It shows disregard for promises
It indicates a political alliance
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the fulfillment of a sworn covenant
questions.explanation: Judges 14:19 describes Samson rewarding those who solved his riddle with thirty garments, fulfilling the terms of his covenantal promise, which reflects the biblical principle of keeping vows and honesty in commitments.

questions.question: What redemptive narrative connection can be drawn from Samson’s conflict with the Philistines in Judges 14:1-20?
options: It anticipates Israel’s final defeat by enemies
It foreshadows the ultimate deliverance through Christ over evil
It depicts the futility of human strength
It promotes intermarriage with foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the ultimate deliverance through Christ over evil
questions.explanation: Samson’s battles against the Philistines (Judges 14:1-20) typologically point forward to Christ’s ultimate victory over evil and deliverance of God’s people, fitting the broader redemption story.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human sin and its consequences is illustrated by Samson’s marriage to a Philistine woman despite parental warning (Judges 14:2-3)?
options: Sin has no real consequences
Human disobedience can be used by God for His purposes but often leads to complications
Sin always leads to immediate destruction
Obedience is irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Human disobedience can be used by God for His purposes but often leads to complications
questions.explanation: Judges 14:2-3 shows Samson’s disregard for parental counsel to avoid marrying an uncircumcised woman, illustrating how human sin can bring difficulties while God’s sovereign plan may still work through flawed human actions.

questions.question: How does the riddle in Judges 14:14 reveal the biblical theme of paradox in God’s revelation?
options: It shows God’s revelation is straightforward
It reveals that divine truth often involves unexpected paradoxes
It denies the reality of evil
It promotes human wisdom above divine
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that divine truth often involves unexpected paradoxes
questions.explanation: The riddle, ‘Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness’ (Judges 14:14), reflects a paradox where strength produces sweetness, illustrating how God’s truth often comes in unexpected, mysterious forms.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Samson’s wife and the Philistines (Judges 14:15-17) teach about the dangers of human weakness and betrayal within God’s redemptive plan?
options: Human weakness has no effect on God’s plans
Betrayal can threaten but not ultimately thwart divine purposes
Human betrayal always stops God’s work
God condones betrayal for success
questions.correctAnswer: Betrayal can threaten but not ultimately thwart divine purposes
questions.explanation: Judges 14:15-17 shows Samson’s wife being used to extract the riddle’s secret, illustrating how human weakness and betrayal pose threats but do not prevent God’s overarching redemptive plan.

questions.question: How does Judges 14:5-6 and Judges 14:19 combined illustrate the doctrine of sanctification by the Spirit in the life of a believer?
options: The Spirit only empowers believers for personal gain
The Spirit equips believers for God’s mission despite personal flaws
The Spirit works without human cooperation
The Spirit’s presence guarantees sinless living
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit equips believers for God’s mission despite personal flaws
questions.explanation: In Judges 14:5-6 and 14:19, the Spirit empowers Samson first to kill the lion and later to slay thirty men, showing that the Holy Spirit equips flawed individuals for God’s mission, supporting the doctrine of sanctification as divine enablement for service.

questions.question: What apologetic answer does Judges 14:4-20 provide to sceptics who claim God does not intervene in human affairs?
options: God is distant and uninvolved
God sovereignly intervenes through human agents like Samson
Human actions are purely random
God’s intervention is only symbolic
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly intervenes through human agents like Samson
questions.explanation: Judges 14:4-20 shows God’s sovereign intervention through Samson’s Spirit-empowered acts against the Philistines, providing an apologetic response that God actively engages in human history.

questions.question: What does Judges 14:8-9 reveal about God’s provision and the theme of blessing coming from unexpected sources?
options: God’s blessings are always obvious
God can provide nourishment and blessing from unlikely and even dead sources
Blessings cannot arise from hardship
Provision is entirely dependent on human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God can provide nourishment and blessing from unlikely and even dead sources
questions.explanation: Judges 14:8-9 describes honey found in a lion’s carcass, illustrating God’s ability to bring blessing and provision from unexpected and even strange places, a theological theme of divine grace.

questions.question: How do Judges 14:1-3 and Judges 14:20 together illustrate the narrative arc of Israel’s compromised faithfulness and its consequences?
options: Israel’s faithfulness leads to immediate victory
Intermarriage with Philistines leads to relational strife and loss
Faithfulness is irrelevant to God’s plan
Israel’s alliances always strengthen it
questions.correctAnswer: Intermarriage with Philistines leads to relational strife and loss
questions.explanation: Judges 14:1-3 shows Samson marrying a Philistine woman against parental advice, and 14:20 records her being given to his companion, indicating the relational and covenantal breakdown resulting from Israel’s compromised faithfulness.
